scenes.text: *Laid off by AI* at 48. *$300* and 12 AI agents later: *$300,000* a year

scenes.title: Who: *Sam Brown*, 48
lines: Austin, Texas. Laid off nine months earlier. "It was AI-related."
Teamed up with Ben Hooten, 39, a former sales rep, and Dan Crump, 56, a former Marine.
Fathom AI, launched early 2026: a sales tool for medical aesthetics clinics.

scenes.title: The *$300* start
lines: They got a term sheet from venture capitalists and walked away.
Structured as a partnership that pays out the profits.

scenes.title: The *AI* part
lines: Twelve AI agents do the work of a staff.
One runs customer success for a national sales force. Another scans competitors every two hours and files a briefing.
Live Google search data and AI roleplay for sales training.

scenes.title: The *numbers*
lines: About $300,000 in annual recurring revenue within 12 weeks, from records Fortune reviewed.
Gross margins above 90%. Costs under 10% of revenue.
Hooten closed $440,000 in one day, his first day using it in the field.

scenes.label: from *start-up cash* to yearly revenue in 12 weeks

scenes.title: The *lesson*
lines: Three people, no office, no funding, cash-flow positive.
They sell to an industry they already knew. The agents removed the payroll.

scenes.text: Want the *3 agents* you can run for under $20 each? Comment *AGENTS* and follow.
